papers.boundaryReview: Q2 contains six separately marked printed parts. The shipped Q2 identity is retained for its first task, and five new identities restore the remaining parts, including the previously absent 5-mark modelling step (iii). Q5(a)(i) gives 5 to each force diagram. Q5(a)(ii) gives 5 for the shared normal reactions, 5 for acceleration of X and 5 for acceleration of Y: X retains the shared step and original identity, Y has its own 5-mark task. Q4(ii) both speeds share a final 5. Q5(b) both signed p/q pairs, Q7(b)(i) both launch angles and Q10(a)(i) both recurrence values each share a final placement. Q6(a)(i) is one 20-mark optimisation task including cost; Q6(a)(ii) is one comparison. Q9(a)(ii) is one graph, with 5 for each required segment. Required method steps are not separate practice tasks.

papers.markingGuideNote: Use the published scale where printed. For other placements, select the published mark for the required working, then deduct 3 for a mathematical error or 1 for a slip or minor misreading. Select zero where no credit is earned. papers.boundaryReview: Q1(b)(i) gives 5 to each force diagram. Q8(a)(i) gives 5 separately for magnitude and direction: the magnitude retains the shipped identity and direction has a new identity. Q6(i) components are intermediate steps in one requested vector with a shared final 5, so remain together. Q4(iv) is one 15-mark shortest-path task including the length. Q9(b)(i) is one adjacency matrix with one-mark entry deductions; Q9(b)(ii) is a single 10-mark multiplication placement, without a printed marking scale. Q10(a)(ii) both roots share a final 5. Required method steps and network edges are not answer-choice pools.
